title: 고난도 · 비교/변화 (14~15번)
intro: OPIc 14~15번은 과거와 현재의 변화를 비교하거나 사회적 이슈에 대한 의견을 묻는 고난도 문제가 주로 나옵니다. 어려운 시사 어휘보다 '서울에서 가족과 사는 경영학과 대학생'인 내 경험을 예시로 드는 것이 훨씬 자연스럽고 점수도 잘 나옵니다. 우리 아파트, 넷플릭스로 영화 보기, 지하철에서 IU 듣기, 오사카 여행, 할머니 댁이 있는 시골처럼 이미 준비한 이야기를 근거로 재활용하세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장('Oh, that's a big question. Let me think.') → 과거 vs 현재 또는 내 입장 → 이유·차이 2개 → 내 경험 예시 → 마무리 문장('So yeah, that's what I think.')
비교(comparison) 문제는 'In the past, ~ / But these days, ~' 로 시제를 분명히 나눈 뒤 'Personally, I think ~' 로 내 생각을 붙이세요.
의견(opinion) 문제는 입장 → 이유 2개(First / Second) → 내 경험 예시 → 결론 순서를 지키면 논리적으로 들립니다.
어려운 단어 대신 쉬운 구어체를 쓰고, AL은 관계사(which, that)와 감정 표현으로 문장을 자연스럽게 길게 만드세요.

expressions.en: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think.
There are a few big differences.
Things have changed a lot over the years.
expressions.ko: 몇 년 사이에 많은 게 바뀌었어요.

expressions.en: My parents told me that back then, ~.
expressions.note: 직접 경험 못 한 과거를 말하는 방법

expressions.en: That's one of the reasons why ~.

expressions.note: 장단점이 함께 있을 때 쓰는 관용 표현

expressions.en: So yeah, all in all, that's what I think.

questions.en: How has housing in Korea changed over the last 20 years? What are the biggest differences between homes today and homes 20 years ago?
questions.ko: 지난 20년 동안 한국의 주거는 어떻게 변했나요? 오늘날의 집과 20년 전 집의 가장 큰 차이는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a big question. Let me think.' → 20년 전(부모님 이야기: 작은 주택, 연탄, 마당) → 요즘(고층 아파트, 편의시설, 비싼 집값) → 우리 집 예시(10층 아파트, 10년째) → 내 생각 → 'So yeah, ~.'
직접 경험 못 한 과거는 'My parents told me that back then, ~' 로 부모님 이야기를 빌리면 자연스럽습니다.
차이를 2개(건물 형태, 집값 또는 편의시설)로 좁혀 말하면 논리적으로 들립니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think. In the past, many people lived in small houses. My parents told me their homes had a small yard. But these days, most people in Seoul live in tall apartments. For example, my family lives on the tenth floor of an apartment building. There's a gym and a parking lot. But houses are much more expensive now. Yeah, that's how housing has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think. Housing in Korea has changed a lot over the last twenty years, and there are two big differences. First, the type of home is different. My parents told me that back then, a lot of people lived in small houses with a yard, and neighbors knew each other well. But these days, most people in Seoul live in tall apartment buildings. For example, my family has lived on the tenth floor of our apartment for about ten years. Our complex has a parking lot, a small gym, and a playground, so it's really convenient. Second, homes are much more expensive now. My parents say they could never buy our apartment at today's price. Personally, I think apartments are comfortable, but I'm a little worried about buying my own home someday. Yeah, that's how housing has changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think. Honestly, housing in Korea has changed so much over the last twenty years that it's kind of hard to believe. I see two really big differences. First, the type of home people live in is totally different now. My parents told me that back then, a lot of families lived in small houses with little yards, and everyone in the neighborhood knew each other by name. These days, though, especially in Seoul, tall apartment complexes are everywhere. In my case, my family has lived on the tenth floor of the same apartment for about ten years, and our complex has pretty much everything, like a parking lot, a gym, and even a little playground. It's super convenient, but to be honest, I barely know the people living next door. Second, homes have become ridiculously expensive. My dad always jokes that if we had to buy our apartment today, we'd have to live on instant noodles for the rest of our lives. As a college student, that's kind of scary, because I have no idea when I'll be able to afford my own place. So yeah, all in all, homes are more comfortable now, but they're a lot harder to get.

questions.en: How has the movie industry changed over the years? How is the way people watch movies today different from the past, and what do you think about these changes?
questions.ko: 영화 산업은 수년간 어떻게 변했나요? 오늘날 사람들이 영화를 보는 방식은 과거와 어떻게 다르며, 이런 변화에 대해 어떻게 생각하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, the movie industry? Let me think.' → 예전(극장, 비디오 대여점, TV 방영) → 요즘(넷플릭스 같은 스트리밍, 집에서 언제든) → 내 경험(주말 밤 집에서 영화, 가족과 애니메이션) → 내 생각(장단점) → 'So yeah, ~.'
In the past / These days 로 시제를 나누고, 'used to' 로 과거 습관을 말하세요.
AL은 'It's a double-edged sword.' 같은 관용 표현으로 장단점을 정리하면 좋습니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, the movie industry? Let me think. In the past, people usually watched movies at the theater. My parents also used to rent videos from a video store. But these days, people watch movies at home on Netflix. For example, I usually watch comedies or action movies at home on weekend nights. It's much cheaper and more convenient. But I still like the big screen sometimes. Yeah, that's how watching movies has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, the movie industry? Let me think. Things have changed a lot over the years. In the past, if you wanted to see a new movie, you had to go to the theater. My parents told me they also used to rent videos from a small video store in the neighborhood. These days, it's totally different. Most people watch movies at home on streaming services like Netflix. You can watch whatever you want, whenever you want. For example, in my case, I usually watch a comedy or an action movie at home on weekend nights. Recently, I watched an animated movie with my family in the living room, and we all loved it. Personally, I think these changes are great, because it's cheap and convenient. On the other hand, theaters are struggling, and that's a little sad. Yeah, that's what I think about it.
answers.AL: Oh, the movie industry? That's a big question. Let me think. I'd say things have changed a lot, especially in the way people watch movies. In the past, going to the movies was kind of a big event. If you wanted to see something new, you had to go to the theater, and my parents told me they also used to rent videos from a little shop in their neighborhood, and they'd get charged a fee if they returned them late. These days, it's a completely different story. Thanks to streaming services like Netflix, you can watch pretty much any movie from your couch, whenever you feel like it. In my case, that's exactly what I do. On weekend nights, after a busy week of classes, I usually curl up at home and watch a comedy or an action movie. Recently, my whole family watched an animated movie together in the living room, and even my dad got emotional at the end. Personally, I think it's a double-edged sword. On one hand, it's cheap, convenient, and perfect for busy people like me. On the other hand, a lot of theaters are struggling, and I think watching a movie on a huge screen is still a special experience. So yeah, all in all, that's what I think.

questions.en: How has technology changed the way people listen to music? Compare how people listened to music in the past with how they do it now.
questions.ko: 기술은 사람들이 음악을 듣는 방식을 어떻게 바꿨나요? 과거와 지금의 음악 듣는 방식을 비교해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, music and technology? Let me think.' → 예전(CD, 카세트, MP3, 라디오) → 요즘(스트리밍 앱, 무선 이어폰, 추천 기능) → 내 경험(지하철에서 IU, 조깅할 때 플레이리스트) → 내 생각 → 'So yeah, ~.'
차이를 2개(듣는 기기, 음악을 찾는 방법)로 정리하면 논리적으로 들립니다.
부모님이 CD를 모았다는 이야기를 넣으면 과거 파트를 쉽게 채울 수 있습니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, music and technology? Let me think. In the past, people listened to music on CDs or the radio. My mom still has a lot of old CDs at home. But these days, people use music apps on their phones. For example, I listen to K-pop and ballads on the subway every day. I just put on my wireless earphones. It's much more convenient now. Yeah, that's how listening to music has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, music and technology? Let me think. Technology has changed the way we listen to music a lot, and there are two big differences. First, the devices are different. In the past, people listened to music on the radio, cassette tapes, or CDs. My mom still keeps a box of old CDs in the living room, and she says buying a new album was really exciting back then. But these days, everyone just uses a music app on their phone. Second, finding new music is much easier now. The app recommends songs for me, so I find new artists all the time. For example, in my case, I listen to IU and ballads on the subway every morning with my wireless earphones. I also make a playlist for jogging. Personally, I think it's great, but songs feel less special now. Yeah, that's how things have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, music and technology? That's an interesting question. Let me think. I think technology has completely changed the way we listen to music, and I'd point to two main differences. First, the devices we use are totally different. Back in the day, people listened to the radio, cassette tapes, or CDs. My mom still has a whole box of old CDs in the living room, and whenever she pulls one out, she tells me how she used to save up her allowance for weeks just to buy one album. These days, though, all you need is a phone and a music app, and you've got millions of songs in your pocket. Second, the way we discover music has changed. Now the apps recommend songs based on what you already like, so I stumble upon new artists all the time without even trying. In my case, music is basically the soundtrack of my day. I listen to IU and ballads on the subway every morning with my wireless earphones, and I have a special playlist for jogging along the Han River. Personally, I love how easy it is now, but I kind of envy my mom, because each album meant so much more to her. So yeah, all in all, that's how things have changed.

questions.en: What are some problems or concerns that people have about traveling these days? Why do you think these issues have come up?
questions.ko: 요즘 사람들이 여행에 대해 갖는 문제나 걱정은 무엇인가요? 왜 이런 문제가 생겼다고 생각하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a big question. Let me think.' → 입장(요즘 여행의 가장 큰 걱정은 비용과 혼잡) → 이유 2개(물가·항공권 상승, SNS로 유명한 곳에 사람이 몰림) → 내 경험(작년 여름 오사카) → 결론 → 'So yeah, ~.'
왜 그런 문제가 생겼는지도 반드시 말하세요. 'I think it's because ~.'
날씨(태풍) 때문에 계획이 바뀌는 문제를 세 번째 예로 덧붙여도 좋습니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think. I think people have two big concerns about travel these days. First, traveling is really expensive now. Flights and hotels cost a lot. Second, famous places are too crowded. I think it's because of social media. For example, last summer, I went to Osaka with my family. The streets were so crowded, and we waited a long time everywhere. Yeah, that's what I think about it.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think. I think people have two big concerns about traveling these days. First, traveling has become really expensive. Flights, hotels, and even food cost much more than before. As a college student, I have to save money for a long time just to take a short trip. Second, popular places are way too crowded. I think it's because of social media. When a place becomes famous online, everyone wants to go there and take the same photo. For example, last summer, my family and I went to Osaka. We loved the street food, but the streets were so packed that we could barely walk. At Universal Studios, we waited almost two hours for one ride. In conclusion, I think people should travel at less busy times. Yeah, that's what I think about travel problems.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think. In my opinion, the two biggest concerns people have about traveling these days are the cost and the crowds. First of all, traveling has gotten really expensive. Flights, hotels, and even a simple meal cost way more than they did a few years ago. I think it's partly because prices went up everywhere, and partly because so many people started traveling again all at once. As a college student, that hits me pretty hard, since I have to save up for months just for a short trip. Second, famous places have become ridiculously crowded, and I honestly think social media is to blame. Once a spot goes viral, everyone rushes there to take the exact same photo. I actually experienced this myself last summer, when my family and I went to Osaka. The street food was amazing, but the streets were so packed that we could barely move, and at Universal Studios, we waited almost two hours for a single ride. By the end of the day, my brother was completely exhausted. So all in all, I think traveling is still worth it, but people should try going in the off-season. So yeah, that's what I think.

questions.en: Some people prefer working from home, while others prefer working at the office. What are the advantages and disadvantages of each? Which do you prefer, and why?
questions.ko: 재택근무를 선호하는 사람도 있고 사무실 근무를 선호하는 사람도 있습니다. 각각의 장단점은 무엇인가요? 당신은 어느 쪽을 선호하며, 그 이유는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, working from home or at the office? Let me think.' → 각각의 장단점 한두 개 → 내 입장(나는 직접 가는 쪽) → 이유 2개 → 내 경험 예시(고등학교 때 온라인 수업, 지금 대학 수업·조별 과제) → 결론 → 'So yeah, ~.'
대학생이라 회사 경험이 없어도 괜찮습니다. 'As a student, ~' 로 온라인 수업과 학교 수업을 비교해 말하세요.
장점은 'The good thing about ~ is ~', 단점은 'On the other hand, ~' 로 정리하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, working from home or at the office? Let me think. Working from home is comfortable, and you don't have to commute. But it's easy to get lazy. Working at the office is better for teamwork. But commuting can be tiring. As a student, I prefer going to school in person. In high school, I took online classes for a while, and I felt lonely. Yeah, that's why I prefer the office.
answers.IH: Oh, working from home or at the office? Let me think. Both have good and bad points. The good thing about working from home is that you save time. You don't have to take a crowded subway, and you can wear comfortable clothes. On the other hand, it's easy to get lazy, and you can feel lonely. Working at the office is better for teamwork and meeting people, but commuting every day can be really tiring. Personally, I prefer the office, and I have two reasons. First, I focus much better when I'm around other people. Second, I like talking face to face. For example, in high school, I took online classes at home for a while, and I almost fell asleep in front of my laptop every day. Now I go to school in person and do group projects with my friend Minji, and it's way more fun. Yeah, that's why I prefer the office.
answers.AL: Oh, working from home or at the office? That's a big question. Let me think. I think both options have pretty clear pros and cons. The best thing about working from home is that you save so much time. You don't have to squeeze onto a packed subway, and you can work in your pajamas if you want. On the other hand, it's really easy to get distracted, and some people end up feeling isolated. Working at the office is great for teamwork and building relationships, but the daily commute can wear you out. Personally, even though I'm still a student, I'd definitely choose the office, for two reasons. First, I focus a lot better when there are other people around me. Second, I think talking face to face makes it so much easier to share ideas. I actually learned this the hard way in high school, when I had to take online classes from my room for a while. I'd sit at my desk in front of my laptop, and half the time, my mind was somewhere else. These days, I go to campus in person, and working on group projects with my friend Minji in a cafe is way more productive, not to mention more fun. So yeah, all in all, I'd pick the office.

questions.en: Compare living in a big city with living in a small town. Which do you think is better for young people, and why?
questions.ko: 대도시에서 사는 것과 작은 마을에서 사는 것을 비교해 주세요. 젊은 사람들에게는 어느 쪽이 더 좋다고 생각하며, 그 이유는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, city life or small-town life? Let me think.' → 대도시(서울: 편리, 기회, 하지만 비싸고 복잡) → 작은 마을(할머니 댁: 조용, 자연, 하지만 불편) → 내 입장(젊은 사람에겐 도시) → 이유 2개 + 내 경험 → 'So yeah, ~.'
비교 문제지만 마지막에 'Which is better' 에 대한 내 입장을 꼭 말해야 합니다.
서울의 지하철·카페·한강, 할머니 댁이 있는 조용한 시골처럼 이미 준비한 디테일을 활용하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, city life or small-town life? Let me think. I live in Seoul, a really big city. It's very convenient. There are subways, cafes, and stores everywhere. But it's crowded and expensive. My grandparents live in a small town. It's quiet and peaceful, but there aren't many things to do. I think a big city is better for young people. There are more jobs and fun things to do. Yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, city life or small-town life? Let me think. I've lived in Seoul my whole life, so I know city life pretty well. Living in a big city is really convenient. In my neighborhood, the subway station is only five minutes away, and there are cafes and convenience stores everywhere. But it's also crowded, noisy, and expensive. On the other hand, my grandparents live in a small town in the countryside. It's quiet and peaceful, and the air is so fresh. But there aren't many buses, and there's not much to do at night. Personally, I think a big city is better for young people, for two reasons. First, there are many more jobs and chances to learn new things. Second, it's easier to meet people and hang out with friends. For example, my friend Minji and I can go to a new cafe any time. Yeah, that's why I think city life is better.
answers.AL: Oh, city life or small-town life? That's an interesting question. Let me think. I've lived in Seoul my entire life, so I'm definitely a city girl, but I've spent a lot of holidays at my grandparents' place in a small town, so I've seen both sides. The best thing about a big city is how convenient everything is. In my neighborhood, the subway station is just five minutes away, and there's a cafe or a convenience store on literally every corner. The downside is that it's crowded, noisy, and super expensive. A small town is pretty much the opposite. Whenever I visit my grandparents, I'm amazed by how quiet it is and how fresh the air feels. But the buses only come once an hour, and everything closes really early, so there's not much to do at night. Personally, I think a big city is better for young people, for two main reasons. First, there are way more job opportunities, which matters a lot to me as a business major. Second, it's so much easier to meet new people and try new things. For example, my friend Minji and I can find a new cafe or restaurant pretty much every weekend. So yeah, all in all, that's why I'd choose the city.

pronunciation.tip: 앞 '인'에 강세. '인더스트리'로 둘째 음절에 힘주지 않기
